title: Go: Select Statement
description: Use the select statement to handle multiple channel operations concurrently.

steps.title: Basic select
steps.description: Create two channels `ch1` and `ch2`. Send "A" on ch1 and "B" on ch2 from goroutines. Use a `select` to receive from whichever is ready and print the value.
hints: Select picks a random ready case if multiple are ready
Run the select twice to receive both values

verification.failureMessage: Make sure both cases print their received values.

steps.title: Select with default
steps.description: Try to receive from a channel that has no data. Use a `default` case to print "No data ready" instead of blocking.
hints: `default` runs when no other case is ready
Don't send any data on the channel so the default triggers

verification.successMessage: Non-blocking select with default case works!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure the default case prints the expected message.

steps.title: Timeout with select
steps.description: Use a select with `time.After(1 * time.Second)` to implement a timeout when waiting on a slow channel. Print "timed out" if the channel doesn't respond in time.
hints: `time.After(d)` returns a channel that sends after duration d
Combine a channel read case with a `<-time.After(1 * time.Second)` case
Don't send on the data channel so the timeout fires

verification.failureMessage: Use time.After in a case to detect timeout.

steps.title: Select with multiple ready channels
steps.description: Create two channels, send on both immediately from goroutines. Use a select in a loop to read 2 values. Print each received value with its source ("Got from ch1: ..." or "Got from ch2: ...").
hints: Both channels will be ready simultaneously
Select picks randomly among ready cases — order may vary
Loop the select twice to drain both channels

verification.successMessage: You handled multiple ready channels with select!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure to print which channel each value came from.

steps.title: Select with nil channels
steps.description: Create a channel and set it to `nil` after receiving from it. Use select to skip nil channels (they are never ready). Print "ch is nil" when the nil case is skipped.
hints: Reading from a nil channel blocks forever — it is never select-ready
Assign `ch = nil` after receiving to disable that case in select
This is useful for dynamically enabling/disabling channel cases

verification.successMessage: Nil channels are silently ignored by select!
verification.failureMessage: Set the channel to nil after receiving from it.
